intro.can: Talk about the delivery in Spanish: describe what you saw on a pitch, ask what the pitcher felt, and suggest one adjustment to test.
intro.can_tr: Hablar de la entrega en español: describir lo que viste en un lanzamiento, preguntar qué sintió el pícher y sugerir un ajuste para probar.

outcomes.es: Nombrar las partes de la entrega: balance, postura, caderas, hombros, paso, brazo, punto de salida.
outcomes.en: Name the parts of the delivery: balance, posture, hips, shoulders, stride, arm, release point.

outcomes.es: Describir un lanzamiento: "Noté que… / Me pareció que…"
outcomes.en: Describe one pitch: "Noté que… / Me pareció que…"

outcomes.es: Evitar las reglas universales y proponer una prueba: "Vamos a probar…", "¿Qué tal si…?"
outcomes.en: Avoid universal rules and propose a test: "Vamos a probar…", "¿Qué tal si…?"

visual.title: Delivery and mechanics
visual.sub: Observe, ask, and test — in Spanish

cues.text: In this lesson, you will learn to talk about the delivery in Spanish: balance, direction, the hips and shoulders, the stride, the arm, and the release.
More important, you will learn how to say it: describe what you saw on one pitch, ask what he felt, and suggest one adjustment to test.

visual.title: The body
visual.note_en: "El balance" is common in Caribbean baseball Spanish; "el equilibrio" is the standard word. Both are understood.

cues.text: Start with the body. Listen and repeat.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el balance… el equilibrio

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la postura

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: las caderas y los hombros

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el lado de adelante

visual.title: The delivery

steps.es: el brazo / el ángulo del brazo
el punto de salida / donde sueltas la pelota
steps.en: the release point / where you let go of the ball

visual.note_en: "El timing" and "el ritmo" (tempo) are both heard. Which Spanish term for release point is standard is not settled; describing it — "donde sueltas la pelota" — is always clear.

cues.text: Now the delivery, from start to finish.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: levantar la pierna

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el paso… la zancada
The second word is correct but formal. With players, the first is more common.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la dirección al plato

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el brazo… el ángulo del brazo

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el punto de salida
With players, describing it is often clearer.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: donde sueltas la pelota
cues.en: where you let go of the ball

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: terminar el lanzamiento

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el ritmo… el timing

visual.title: Let's work on it

rows.example: Vamos a trabajar en tu balance.
Mantén la dirección hacia el plato.
rows.en: Keep your direction toward the plate.

visual.note_en: "Vamos a…" (let's…) makes the work shared and fits both tú and usted. Usted forms: mantenga, pruebe.

cues.text: The most useful frame in coaching Spanish means let's. It makes the work something you do together.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Vamos a trabajar en tu balance.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Vamos a revisar el video.
For one short cue before a pitch, an instruction is fine.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Mantén la dirección hacia el plato.
cues.en: Keep your direction toward the plate.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Prueba ese ajuste otra vez.

visual.title: Observation, not a rule

items.es: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en ese lanzamiento.
items.en: It looked to me like your front side opened early on that pitch.

items.es: Siempre tienes que mantener el lado de adelante cerrado.
items.en: You always have to keep your front side closed. (A universal rule — avoid it.)

visual.note_en: An observation is about one pitch, in the past tense: "se abrió" (it opened). "Siempre tienes que…" (you always have to…) turns it into a rule for every pitch and every pitcher.

cues.text: After a rep, describe what you saw on that pitch. Start with: I noticed, or, it looked to me like.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Noté que…

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Me pareció que…

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en ese lanzamiento.
cues.en: It looked to me like your front side opened early on that pitch.

cues.text: The verb is in the past. It happened on that pitch. You are describing one rep, not judging the pitcher.
Now compare it with this sentence.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Siempre tienes que mantener el lado de adelante cerrado.
cues.en: You always have to keep your front side closed.

cues.text: Always, and have to. That turns one observation into a universal rule. Mechanics are individual, and no single cue is right for every pitcher, so experienced coaches avoid this kind of sentence.

visual.title: Turn it into a test
visual.note_en: One small change at a time, agreed with the rest of the staff. If something hurts ("¿Te duele?"), stop and involve the medical staff.

cues.text: Instead, propose a test.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Vamos a probar mantener el lado de adelante cerrado un poquito más.
cues.en: Let's try keeping your front side closed a little longer.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: ¿Qué tal si apuntas el pie hacia el cátcher?
cues.en: What if you point your foot at the catcher?

cues.text: Or give him something outside the body to focus on.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Fíjate en el guante del cátcher.
After the rep, check the feel, and let him locate the release himself.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: ¿Sentiste alguna diferencia?

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: ¿Dónde estás soltando la pelota?
cues.en: Where are you letting go of the ball?

cues.text: Keep changes small, one at a time, and part of the plan you share with the rest of the staff. Ask about discomfort, and never push a change that hurts.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: ¿Te molesta algo?

visual.title: The illustrated rep
visual.caption: Illustration — not a real pitcher, not a mechanical diagnosis
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: no es un pícher real ni un diagnóstico mecánico.

cues.text: Here is an illustrated rep. It is a drawing, not a real pitcher, and not a diagnosis. In this drawing, the front side opens early.
Listen to how Coach Alex talks about it: what he saw, then a question.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: En ese lanzamiento, me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano.
cues.en: On that pitch, it looked to me like your front side opened early.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: ¿Qué sentiste?

cues.speaker: luis
cues.text: Sentí que el brazo llegó un poco tarde.
cues.en: It felt like my arm got there a little late.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Vamos a probar algo. Fíjate en el guante del cátcher y mantén el hombro de adelante cerrado un poquito más.
cues.en: Let's try something. Focus on the catcher's glove and keep your front shoulder closed a little longer.

visual.title: The next rep
visual.caption: Illustration — not a real pitcher, not a mechanical diagnosis
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: no es un pícher real ni un diagnóstico mecánico.

cues.text: In the second drawing, the front side stays closed a little longer. Coach Alex describes it and checks the feel.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Ahí se quedó cerrado un poquito más. ¿Sentiste alguna diferencia?
cues.en: There it stayed closed a little longer. Did you feel any difference?

cues.speaker: luis
cues.text: Sí, sentí el brazo más suelto.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Bien. Vamos a revisar el video, y después prueba ese ajuste otra vez.
cues.en: Good. Let's look at the video, and then try that adjustment again.

cues.text: Describe what happened, ask what he felt, suggest one thing to test, and say what you will check on the next rep. That is exactly what you will do in the conversation at the end of this lesson.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Luis, hoy vamos a trabajar en tu balance. Nada más eso.
lines.en: Luis, today we're going to work on your balance. Just that.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Con la recta nada más, coach?
lines.en: Just fastballs, Coach?

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Sí, diez rectas. Fíjate en el guante del cátcher y mantén la dirección hacia el plato.
lines.en: Yes, ten fastballs. Focus on the catcher's glove and keep your direction toward the plate.

lines.speaker: ana
lines.text: Coach, yo voy a grabar el video desde el lado.
lines.en: Coach, I'll record the video from the side.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Perfecto, Ana. Después lo revisamos juntos, Luis.
lines.en: Perfect, Ana. Afterwards we'll look at it together, Luis.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Luis, ¿qué sentiste en esa?
lines.en: Luis, what did you feel on that one?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: No sé, coach. Sentí que el brazo llegó tarde.
lines.en: I don't know, Coach. It felt like my arm was late.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió un poco temprano. Vamos a revisar el video.
lines.en: It looked to me like your front side opened a little early. Let's look at the video.

lines.speaker: ana
lines.text: Aquí está, coach. Mira el hombro de adelante.
lines.en: Here it is, Coach. Look at the front shoulder.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Sí. ¿Qué tal si mantienes el hombro cerrado un poquito más? Prueba ese ajuste en las próximas tres.
lines.en: Yes. What if you keep your shoulder closed a little longer? Try that adjustment on the next three.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok, coach.
lines.en: OK, Coach.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Noté que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en ese lanzamiento.
lines.en: I noticed your front side opened early on that pitch.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: ¿Sentiste alguna diferencia? Prueba ese ajuste otra vez.
lines.en: Did you feel any difference? Try that adjustment again.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, ¿cómo estuvo esa?
lines.en: Coach, how was that one?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, ¿tengo que cambiar mi mecánica?
lines.en: Coach, do I have to change my mechanics?

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Vamos a revisar el video.
lines.en: Let's look at the video.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, ¿qué viste en esa?
lines.en: Coach, what did you see on that one?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ah, ok. ¿El lado de adelante se abrió temprano?
lines.en: Oh, OK. My front side opened early?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Perdón, coach, no te entendí. ¿Qué pasó en esa?
lines.en: Sorry, Coach, I didn't understand. What happened on that one?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Yo no me di cuenta.
lines.en: I didn't notice.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Sentí que el brazo llegó un poco tarde.
lines.en: It felt like my arm got there a little late.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Cómo, coach? ¿Qué me preguntaste?
lines.en: Sorry, Coach? What did you ask me?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Y qué hago diferente en la próxima?
lines.en: So what do I do differently on the next one?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok, vamos a probar eso.
lines.en: OK, let's try that.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Perdón, ¿qué quieres que pruebe?
lines.en: Sorry, what do you want me to try?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Listo, coach. ¿En qué me fijo en esta?
lines.en: Ready, Coach. What should I pay attention to on this one?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok. Después te digo si sentí la diferencia.
lines.en: OK. I'll tell you afterwards if I felt the difference.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Perdón, coach, ¿en qué me tengo que fijar?
lines.en: Sorry, Coach, what should I be paying attention to?

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish word with its meaning.
activities.explain_en: "El paso" is the everyday word for the stride; "la zancada" is correct but formal. For the release point, "donde sueltas la pelota" (where you let go of the ball) is the clearest with players.

figure.caption: Body words on a schematic delivery at foot strike.

activities.intro: Coach Alex sets up a bullpen with Luis and Ana. Listen and answer.

questions.prompt: What is the one focus for today?
questions.explain: "Hoy vamos a trabajar en tu balance. Nada más eso." One objective for the session.

questions.prompt: What will Luis throw, and what should he focus on?
options: Ten fastballs, focusing on the catcher's glove
Ten sliders, focusing on his hips
Five fastballs, focusing on his stride
questions.explain: "Diez rectas. Fíjate en el guante del cátcher…": ten fastballs; focus on the catcher's glove.

questions.prompt: What will happen with the video?
options: Ana records it, and they look at it together afterwards.
questions.explain: Ana: "Voy a grabar el video." Alex: "Después lo revisamos juntos."

activities.intro: After a rep, Coach Alex talks with Luis. Ana has the video. Listen and answer.

questions.explain: "Sentí que el brazo llegó tarde": it felt like my arm was late.

questions.prompt: How does Coach Alex describe what he saw?
options: As an observation about that pitch: the front side opened a little early
As a rule Luis must always follow
He doesn't say what he saw
questions.explain: "Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió un poco temprano": it looked to me like… — one pitch, past tense.

options: Try keeping the shoulder closed a little longer on the next three
Change his arm angle for the rest of the season
questions.explain: "¿Qué tal si mantienes el hombro cerrado un poquito más? Prueba ese ajuste en las próximas tres." A test, not a decree.

activities.explain: "Las caderas" = the hips. "Los hombros" = the shoulders. "Las rodillas" = the knees.

activities.prompt: Which phrase means the stride in everyday field talk?
activities.explain: "El paso" is the everyday word; "la zancada" is correct but formal. "El plato" is home plate; "el guante" is the glove.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is an observation about one pitch?
options: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano.
Siempre tienes que mantener el lado de adelante cerrado.
Nunca abras el lado de adelante.
activities.explain: "Me pareció que… se abrió" describes what you saw on that pitch. The other two are universal rules: "always you have to…" and "never open…".

activities.prompt: Build the sentence: "Let's work on your balance."
answers: vamos a trabajar en tu balance
activities.explain_en: "Vamos a" + verb = let's… Note "trabajar en" (work on).

activities.prompt: Why do experienced coaches avoid "Siempre tienes que…" when talking about mechanics?
options: It presents one cue as right for every pitcher and every pitch.
It is too informal for academy players.
activities.explain: The Spanish is correct. The problem is the message: mechanics are individual, so a cue is something to test, not a law.

activities.prompt: Turn the rule into a test. Which is best?
options: Vamos a probar mantener el lado de adelante cerrado un poquito más.
Tienes que cerrar el lado de adelante.
activities.explain: "Vamos a probar…" (let's try…) proposes a small change you'll check together; "un poquito más" keeps it small.

activities.prompt: Build the question: "Did you feel any difference?"
activities.explain_en: "¿Sentiste…?" = did you feel…? (past). "Alguna diferencia" = any difference.

activities.prompt: You're working with a veteran reliever in his thirties whom you've just met. Which is the most respectful way to suggest a test?
options: ¿Qué tal si prueba el mismo ajuste otra vez?
activities.explain: After "¿Qué tal si…?", "prueba" here is the usted form (with tú it would be "pruebas"): respectful with an older player you don't know yet. "Vamos a probar…" works with anyone. Guidance, not a rule.

activities.prompt: After trying a change, Luis says his elbow hurts. What do you say first?
options: ¿Te duele? Paramos aquí y hablamos con el personal médico.
activities.explain: Pain ends the test: stop, and bring in the medical staff. "¿Te duele?" = does it hurt? "Paramos aquí" = we'll stop here.

activities.prompt: Build the sentence: "Keep your direction toward the plate."
activities.en: Keep your direction toward the plate.
answers: mantén la dirección hacia el plato
activities.explain_en: "Mantén" (keep, tú) — usted: "mantenga". "Hacia el plato" = toward the plate.

activities.prompt: Complete the observation: "Noté que el lado de adelante se ___ temprano."
activities.explain: "Se abrió" (it opened) is past: it happened on that pitch. "Se abre siempre" (it always opens) generalizes; "abrir" is the infinitive.

activities.text: Noté que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en ese lanzamiento.
activities.en: I noticed your front side opened early on that pitch.
activities.tip_en: Stress the last syllable of "abrió" and "noté" — the accent mark shows where. That ending is what makes it past tense.

figure.caption: Observation: the front shoulder opened early on this rep.

activities.text: ¿Sentiste alguna diferencia? Prueba ese ajuste otra vez.
activities.en: Did you feel any difference? Try that adjustment again.
activities.tip_en: "Ajuste": the j is a soft h sound from the throat, "a-HOOS-te".

activities.goal: The learner gives brief feedback on the last pitch framed as an observation of that pitch (noté que / me pareció que + past tense, e.g. the front side opened early, good balance, good direction), and/or asks what he felt. A universal rule (siempre tienes que…, nunca…) does not meet the goal. Accept any reasonable mechanical observation; don't require exact wording.
activities.goal_en: Describe one thing you saw on that pitch, as an observation — and/or ask what he felt.
examples: Buena. Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió un poco temprano. ¿Qué sentiste?
Noté que tu balance estuvo mejor en esa. ¿Cómo te sentiste?
Bien. ¿Qué sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?

activities.prompt_en: Coach, do I have to change my mechanics?
activities.goal: The learner reassures the pitcher that this is not a required overhaul, and frames any change as one small test to try and check by feel (vamos a probar…, ¿qué tal si…?, después me dices cómo te sientes). Must not present a cue as mandatory or universal.
activities.goal_en: Reassure him, and frame it as one small test you'll check together.
examples: No, no tienes que cambiar todo. Vamos a probar un ajuste pequeño y me dices cómo te sientes.
No. ¿Qué tal si probamos mantener el lado de adelante cerrado un poquito más? Después revisamos el video.
Nada grande. Vamos a probar una cosa, y si no te sientes cómodo, la dejamos.

activities.setting: Bullpen session. You and Luis have just looked at the illustrated rep on the tablet (a drawing made by the app, not a real pitcher and not a diagnosis): in it, his front side opens early. Talk it through with him in Spanish, using tú.
activities.objective: Describe what happened on that rep, ask what he felt, suggest one adjustment to try, and say what you'll check on the next rep.

turns.en: Coach, what did you see on that one?
turns.goal: Describe what happened on that rep as an observation in the past tense (e.g. the front side / front shoulder opened early: el lado de adelante se abrió temprano), not as a universal rule.
turns.goal_en: Describe what happened on that rep, as an observation.
examples: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en esa.
Noté que el hombro de adelante se abrió un poco temprano.

options: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en esa.
Siempre tienes que mantener el lado de adelante cerrado.
Vamos a comer a las doce.

ack.line: Ah, ok. ¿El lado de adelante se abrió temprano?
ack.en: Oh, OK. My front side opened early?

clarify.line: Perdón, coach, no te entendí. ¿Qué pasó en esa?
clarify.en: Sorry, Coach, I didn't understand. What happened on that one?

turns.goal: Ask the pitcher what he felt on that pitch (e.g. ¿Qué sentiste? ¿Cómo te sentiste en esa? ¿Qué sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?).
turns.goal_en: Ask Luis what he felt on that pitch.
examples: No hay problema. ¿Cómo te sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?

ack.line: Sentí que el brazo llegó un poco tarde.
ack.en: It felt like my arm got there a little late.

clarify.en: Sorry, Coach? What did you ask me?

turns.line: ¿Y qué hago diferente en la próxima?
turns.en: So what do I do differently on the next one?
turns.goal: Suggest one adjustment to try, framed as a test (vamos a probar…, ¿qué tal si…?, prueba…), e.g. keep the front side or shoulder closed a little longer, focus on the catcher's glove, keep direction to the plate. One change only; nothing presented as mandatory.
turns.goal_en: Suggest one adjustment to try — as a test.
examples: Vamos a probar mantener el lado de adelante cerrado un poquito más.
¿Qué tal si te fijas en el guante del cátcher y mantienes el hombro cerrado un poquito más?

options: Vamos a probar mantener el lado de adelante cerrado un poquito más.
Cambia todo: el brazo, el paso y las caderas.
Nunca abras el lado de adelante.

clarify.en: Sorry, what do you want me to try?

turns.line: Listo, coach. ¿En qué me fijo en esta?
turns.en: Ready, Coach. What should I pay attention to on this one?
turns.goal: Say what you will check on the next rep (e.g. the front side / shoulder, direction to the plate, where he releases the ball) and/or ask him to tell you afterwards whether he felt a difference. Mentioning reviewing the video is a plus.
turns.goal_en: Say what you'll check on the next rep, and ask him to tell you how it felt.
examples: Voy a mirar el lado de adelante. Después me dices si sentiste alguna diferencia.
Fíjate en el guante del cátcher. Yo miro el hombro, y después revisamos el video.

options: Voy a mirar el lado de adelante. Después me dices si sentiste alguna diferencia.

ack.line: Ok. Después te digo si sentí la diferencia.
ack.en: OK. I'll tell you afterwards if I felt the difference.

clarify.line: Perdón, coach, ¿en qué me tengo que fijar?
clarify.en: Sorry, Coach, what should I be paying attention to?

items.explain: "Soltar" = let go. Where you let go of the ball = the release point ("el punto de salida").

items.prompt: Which sentence describes one pitch instead of making a rule?
options: Noté que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano.
Siempre tienes que mantener el lado de adelante cerrado.
items.explain: "Noté que… se abrió": past tense, one pitch.

items.prompt: "¿Qué tal si apuntas el pie hacia el cátcher?" is…
items.explain: "¿Qué tal si…?" (what if…?) proposes something to try.

items.prompt: Listen. What does Coach Alex say?
items.explain: "Vamos a revisar el video": let's look at the video.

phrases.es: Vamos a trabajar en tu balance.
phrases.note: "Balance" is common in Caribbean baseball Spanish; "equilibrio" is the standard word.

phrases.es: Mantén la dirección hacia el plato.
phrases.en: Keep your direction toward the plate.

phrases.es: Me pareció que el lado de adelante se abrió temprano en ese lanzamiento.
phrases.en: It looked to me like your front side opened early on that pitch.
phrases.note: "Alante" for "adelante" is common colloquial Caribbean speech.

phrases.en: Where are you letting go of the ball?
phrases.note: Describing the release is clearer with players than "el punto de salida", whose standard form is unverified.
Works with both tú and usted.

phrases.es: Fíjate en el guante del cátcher.

phrases.en: Is anything bothering you? / Does it hurt?
phrases.note: Ask both: discomfort and pain are different questions.
"La zancada" is correct but formal; "el paso" is the field word.
